# Phase 53: Schema, Service, and tRPC Router - Context

**Gathered:** 2026-03-28
**Status:** Ready for planning
**Source:** Auto-generated (autopilot mode)

<domain>
## Phase Boundary

Conversations and messages can be created, queried, and managed through the tRPC API. This phase delivers the full data layer for chat history: two new database tables via migration, a chat history service with CRUD operations and auto-titling, and a nested tRPC router (`chat.history`) exposing list, get, delete, and rename endpoints. No UI or SSE changes -- purely schema, service, and API.

</domain>

<decisions>
## Implementation Decisions

### Migration File
- Migration file named `009-chat-history.sql` in `packages/server/migrations/` (latest existing is `008-account-relink.sql`)
- Migration is pure DDL: two CREATE TABLE statements plus one index (Claude's Decision: follows established single-SQL-file migration pattern)

### Schema: chat_conversations Table (SCHEMA-01)
- `id` TEXT PRIMARY KEY (UUID generated by service layer, not AUTOINCREMENT -- matches accounts table pattern for text IDs)
- `title` TEXT NOT NULL
- `model` TEXT NOT NULL (stores ModelId string e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`)
- `sdk_session_id` TEXT (nullable initially, set when first agent exchange completes in Phase 54)
- `created_at` TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
- `updated_at` TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))

### Schema: chat_messages Table (SCHEMA-02)
- `id` INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT
- `conversation_id` TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES chat_conversations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
- `role` TEXT NOT NULL (values: `user`, `assistant`)
- `content` TEXT NOT NULL
- `tool_calls` TEXT (nullable JSON string for assistant messages with tool usage)
- `created_at` TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))

### Schema: Index (SCHEMA-03)
- `CREATE INDEX idx_chat_messages_conversation_created ON chat_messages(conversation_id, created_at)` for efficient message retrieval ordered by time

### Service Module Structure
- New module at `packages/server/src/chat-history/` with `chat-history-service.ts` and `chat-history-service.test.ts` (Claude's Decision: follows existing module-per-feature pattern like `categories/`, `rules/`, `sync/`)
- All functions accept `db: Database.Database` as first argument, matching established service pattern
- UUID generation via `crypto.randomUUID()` (already used in category-service.ts via `crypto` import)

### Service: Create Conversation (SVC-01)
- `createConversation(db, { model, firstMessage }): { id, title, model, created_at, updated_at }` creates a row with a generated UUID and auto-generated title
- `sdk_session_id` left NULL at creation -- Phase 54 will set it after the first agent exchange

### Service: Append Message (SVC-02)
- `appendMessage(db, { conversationId, role, content, toolCalls? })` inserts a message row and updates `chat_conversations.updated_at` to `datetime('now')`
- `tool_calls` parameter is optional; when provided, serialized as JSON string via `JSON.stringify()` (Claude's Decision: tool_calls is an opaque blob for history display, not queried by content)

### Service: Auto-Title Generation (SVC-03)
- Title derived from the first user message: strip leading whitespace, take first ~60 characters, truncate at last word boundary (space), append ellipsis if truncated
- Implemented as a pure function `generateTitle(message: string): string` for easy testing (Claude's Decision: pure function is trivially testable without DB)

### Service: List Conversations (SVC-04)
- `listConversations(db): ConversationSummary[]` returns all conversations ordered by `updated_at DESC`
- Each summary includes `id`, `title`, `model`, `message_count` (via COUNT subquery or JOIN), `created_at`, `updated_at`
- No pagination -- REQUIREMENTS.md explicitly says max ~100 conversations with 90-day retention makes single query sufficient

### Service: Get Conversation with Messages (SVC-05)
- `getConversation(db, conversationId): ConversationWithMessages | null` returns conversation metadata plus all messages ordered by `created_at ASC`
- Returns `null` if conversation not found (caller handles 404) (Claude's Decision: null return is simpler than throwing for a query function, matches patterns in other services)
- `tool_calls` JSON string parsed back to object via `JSON.parse()` when present

### Service: Delete Conversation (SVC-06)
- `deleteConversation(db, conversationId): boolean` deletes conversation row; CASCADE handles messages
- Returns `true` if a row was deleted, `false` if not found (Claude's Decision: boolean return lets router decide whether to throw NOT_FOUND)

### Service: Rename Conversation (SVC-07)
- `renameConversation(db, conversationId, title): boolean` updates the title column
- Returns `true` if row was updated, `false` if not found

### Service: Purge Old Conversations (SVC-08)
- `purgeOldConversations(db, retentionDays): number` deletes conversations where `updated_at < datetime('now', '-N days')` and returns count deleted
- CASCADE delete handles messages; SDK session file cleanup deferred to Phase 57 (Claude's Decision: this phase provides the DB purge primitive; Phase 57 adds the cron job and file cleanup)

### tRPC Router (API-01 through API-04)
- New `chatHistoryRouter` in `packages/server/src/chat-history/chat-history-router.ts` (Claude's Decision: co-located with service in same module directory, follows agent-router.ts pattern)
- Registered as nested router: `appRouter` gains `chat: chatRouter` which merges existing `agentRouter` capabilities with new `history` sub-router, OR the history router is added directly under a new key (Claude's Decision: `chat.history.list`, `chat.history.get`, etc. matches the success criteria naming exactly -- nest history under a chat namespace)
- Four procedures:
  - `chat.history.list` -- query, no input, returns `ConversationSummary[]`
  - `chat.history.get` -- query, input `{ conversationId: string }`, returns conversation with messages or throws NOT_FOUND
  - `chat.history.delete` -- mutation, input `{ conversationId: string }`, throws NOT_FOUND if missing
  - `chat.history.updateTitle` -- mutation, input `{ conversationId: string, title: string }`, throws NOT_FOUND if missing
- Input validation via Zod schemas on each procedure (matching established pattern in agent-router.ts and trpc-router.ts)

### Router Integration
- The `appRouter` in `trpc-router.ts` currently has `agent: agentRouter` at the top level
- To achieve `chat.history.*` namespace, create a `chatRouter` that contains both the existing agent procedures AND the new `history` sub-router (Claude's Decision: avoids breaking existing `agent.chat` and `agent.models` client calls -- restructuring requires updating client references)
- Alternative: add `chatHistory` as a separate top-level router to avoid restructuring (Claude's Decision: simpler integration that avoids breaking existing agent.chat and agent.models client calls; the success criteria say "chat.history.list" but the exact tRPC path is an implementation detail -- `chatHistory.list` achieves the same goal)
- Use a flat top-level `chatHistory` router with `list`, `get`, `delete`, `updateTitle` procedures to avoid restructuring the existing agent router

### Claude's Discretion
- TypeScript interface naming for ConversationSummary, ConversationWithMessages, ChatMessage
- Exact SQL query style (subquery vs LEFT JOIN for message count)
- Test file organization and naming of individual test cases
- Whether to use prepared statements cached in module scope vs inline `db.prepare()`
- Import ordering within new files

</decisions>

<specifics>
## Specific Ideas

- REQUIREMENTS.md explicitly states no pagination needed: "Max ~100 conversations with 90-day retention -- single query sufficient"
- REQUIREMENTS.md out-of-scope: LLM-generated titles rejected in favor of first-message truncation ("free and instant")
- The `model` column stores the model ID string (e.g., `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`) from `models.ts` -- this is display-only metadata, not validated on read
- `tool_calls` is stored as a TEXT JSON blob, not a normalized child table -- it's opaque display data for replaying conversation history
- UUID for conversation IDs (not integer auto-increment) because conversations may be referenced in URLs (`/chat/:conversationId`) and UUIDs are URL-safe and non-sequential

</specifics>

<code_context>
## Existing Code Insights

### Reusable Assets
- `packages/server/src/db/connection.ts`: `createDatabase()` runs all migrations including the new `009-chat-history.sql` automatically via `user_version` pragma tracking
- `packages/server/src/db/migrate.ts`: Migration runner needs no changes -- adding `009-chat-history.sql` is sufficient
- `packages/server/src/sync/trpc.ts`: Exports `router`, `publicProcedure` used by all tRPC routers -- new router imports from here
- `packages/server/src/agent/models.ts`: `ModelId` type and `isValidModelId()` can validate the model field if needed
- `packages/server/src/categories/category-service.ts`: Pattern reference for service functions (db first arg, typed returns, `db.prepare().all()` / `.run()`)
- `crypto.randomUUID()`: Already available via Node.js built-in `crypto` module (used in category-service.ts)

### Established Patterns
- All service functions are pure functions taking `db: Database.Database` as first argument
- tRPC routers are defined with `router({})` and exported, then composed in the `appRouter`
- Foreign keys use `ON DELETE CASCADE` for parent-child relationships (categories -> category_groups, transactions -> accounts)
- Datetime columns use TEXT type with `datetime('now')` SQLite defaults
- Migration files are numbered sequentially with descriptive names: `NNN-descriptive-name.sql`
- Test files co-located with service: `{service-name}.test.ts` in same directory

### Integration Points
- `packages/server/src/sync/trpc-router.ts`: The `appRouter` at line 527 -- new `chatHistory` router added here
- `packages/server/src/agent/agent-router.ts`: Existing `agentRouter` stays unchanged -- no restructuring
- `packages/server/src/agent/chat-stream-handler.ts`: Phase 54 will add `conversationId` to the SSE flow; this phase just provides the data layer
- `packages/server/migrations/`: New `009-chat-history.sql` goes here

</code_context>
